extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on how Title IX obligations interact with FERPA and constitutional due process, including when Title IX or constitutional rights override FERPA, what evidence must be disclosed or redacted in grievance procedures, and special rules for coordinators, minors, students with disabilities, and different types of recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: GEPA override
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a direct conflict between Title IX and FERPA, Title IX overrides FERPA pursuant to GEPA (20 U.S.C. 1221(d)); the obligation to comply with Title IX is not obviated or alleviated by FERPA (§106.6(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This override is statutorily mandated and incorporated into §106.6(e); recipients must not use FERPA as a shield from compliance with Title IX. Whether a direct conflict arises is fact-specific and must be resolved case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional override (due process)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department cannot administer, enforce, or interpret Title IX or FERPA in a manner that would require a recipient to deny parties their constitutional due process rights; where provisions necessary to protect due process rights conflict with FERPA, the Constitution overrides FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is reflected in §106.6(d) and the Department's prior guidance; Mathews v. Eldridge establishes that procedural due process requires notice and a meaningful opportunity to respond. Thus Title IX provisions needed to protect due process (e.g., access to evidence) prevail over FERPA when in direct conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with both Title IX and FERPA absent direct conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must fulfill its obligations under both Title IX and FERPA unless a direct conflict precludes compliance with both laws and their regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should interpret Title IX and FERPA to avoid conflicts when possible. The Department maintains the position that recipients should not use FERPA to avoid Title IX obligations and that determinations about conflicts are fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to evidence relevant to allegations (relevant & not otherwise impermissible)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide the parties with access to the evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex discrimination and not otherwise impermissible (§§106.45(f)(4), 106.46(e)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient must not redact information or evidence that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible because such redaction would infringe on parties' rights to access relevant evidence and on due process. When disclosure of personally identifiable information from education records is directly conflicted by FERPA, the GEPA and/or constitutional overrides justify disclosure of unredacted relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of evidence that are impermissible regardless of relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX grievance procedures must exclude three types of evidence and questions seeking that evidence: evidence protected under a privilege or confidentiality; records made or maintained by a physician, psychologist, or other recognized professional in connection with treatment; and evidence relating to the complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct (with narrow exceptions) (§106.45(b)(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence in these categories is considered impermissible and must not be accessed, considered, disclosed, or otherwise used regardless of whether it is relevant to the allegations, except as narrowly provided in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must redact (or otherwise refrain from disclosing) information that is impermissible under §106.45(b)(7), but must not redact information that is relevant to the allegations and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FERPA would require redactions that preclude compliance with Title IX obligations (e.g., preventing meaningful access to relevant evidence), the GEPA override requires compliance with Title IX. The Department views due process and fundamental fairness as requiring disclosure of unredacted information that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible, even if inconsistent with FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA and disciplinary/witness statement disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA precedent recognizes that a parent or eligible student has a right to inspect any witness statement directly related to the student, even if that statement contains information also directly related to another student, where information cannot be segregated and redacted without destroying its meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Title IX context, there is no direct conflict between Title IX and FERPA regarding the disclosure of information contained in one student's education records to another student to whom that information is also directly related (see prior Dept. guidance and case law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibilities to prevent redisclosure by parties/advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Although FERPA's rules govern recipients' disclosures, they do not authorize or restrict a student from redisclosing their own education records; Title IX regulations require recipients to take reasonable steps to prevent and address unauthorized disclosures by parties and their advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps may include restrictions on the parties' and advisors' ability to redisclose information, training, confidentiality agreements, and other safeguards (§§106.45(f)(4)(iii), 106.46(e)(6)(iii)). The Department rejects applying FERPA's recipient-disclosure rules to private redisclosures by parties/advisors, but expects recipients to mitigate risks of unauthorized redisclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction by type of recipient (elementary/secondary vs postsecondary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX disclosure and grievance-procedure requirements vary based on whether the recipient is an elementary school, secondary school, or postsecondary institution: §106.45 principally governs elementary/secondary, while §106.46 (in addition to §106.45) applies to postsecondary students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification and disclosure requirements differ by recipient type (e.g., notice of allegations, access to evidence, written determinations). Regardless of recipient type, the GEPA and constitutional overrides require compliance with Title IX disclosure duties even when such disclosures conflict with FERPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator access to records for students with disabilities (legitimate educational interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Title IX Coordinator obtains access to personally identifiable information from the education records of a party with a disability to comply with §106.8(e), the Department views this access as a 'legitimate educational interest' under FERPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply with both FERPA and Title IX, a recipient must specify criteria in its annual FERPA notification that permit its Title IX Coordinator to constitute a 'school official' with legitimate educational interests when performing functions to carry out §106.8(e). The Dept. recognizes typical guidance that school officials have a legitimate educational interest when they need to review records to fulfill professional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized legal representatives (§106.6(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'authorized legal representative,' like a parent or guardian, has the right to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other person subject to §106.6(e), including making a complaint and exercising Title IX-related rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declined to define 'authorized legal representative' because terminology and procedures vary by State and context; whether an individual may serve and the scope of authority is determined by State law, court orders, child custody arrangements, or other legal sources. The provision does not confer parental rights on any individual, does not mandate parental notification, and does not alter FERPA inspection and review rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.44(j) confidentiality and limited exceptions for disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(j) prohibits a recipient from disclosing personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with Title IX, with limited exceptions; §106.44(j)(5) allows a recipient to make a disclosure that is permitted by FERPA to the extent such disclosure is not otherwise in conflict with Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERPA permits certain disclosures in limited circumstances (e.g., 34 CFR 99.31). Recipients should consult the discussion of §106.44(j) for details on when personally identifiable information obtained under Title IX may be disclosed and how FERPA-permitted disclosures interact with Title IX obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemptive effect of Title IX regulations (§106.6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.6(b) addresses preemption concerns: recipients may not adopt policies or practices that contravene Title IX or these regulations even if such policies are required by a conflicting State law; Title IX's conditions attach to Federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department maintains that the preemption provision is within its authority under the Spending Clause: recipients who accept Federal education funds agree to comply with federally imposed conditions. States retain the ability to enact laws that do not conflict with federal law. The Dept. will evaluate conflicts consistent with precedent (e.g., Pennhurst) and established principles of preemption and supremacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance on intersections with other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to promote compliance with the final Title IX regulations and to explain their intersection with FERPA and other Federal laws (e.g., IDEA, Section 504, Title VI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Dept. acknowledges requests for resources and guidance on how Title IX interacts with FERPA and other statutes and will provide assistance to help recipients apply the regulations while considering other legal obligations.
